propositions: The test kills its pytest-xdist worker on macOS py3.13 due to exceeding the 300-second per-test timeout: 91.6s idle, 504.8s under CPU saturation (1.7x over budget).
The single monolithic test loop processes 884 corpus units with ~1768 serial pandoc spawns, creating unbounded cost that grows with corpus size.
pytest-timeout with thread method calls os._exit(1) from a timer thread, killing the worker without a traceback or assertion, producing 'node down: Not properly terminated' in xdist logs.
The fix chunks the equivalence test into fixed-size batches (40 units per chunk) using pytest.mark.parametrize, bounding per-test cost to ~4.2s idle and enabling xdist to parallelize.
A new coverage guard test asserts all chunks concatenate to the full renderable unit set and total >= 100, preventing silent unit drops.
All 884 units remain byte-compared against the oracle with real pandoc at stride 1; the parametrization is a structural cost fix, not a test weakening.
